:::{#thm-back-substitution}
#### Solving a triangular system by substitution

Let $\matr{U}$ be an $n \times n$ upper triangular matrix (@def-triangular-matrix)
whose diagonal entries $u_{11}, \ldots, u_{nn}$ are all nonzero.
For every $\vecf{b} \in \reals^n$, the system $\matr{U} \vecf{x} = \vecf{b}$
has exactly one solution, given for $i = n, n - 1, \ldots, 1$ in turn by

$$
x_i = \frac{1}{u_{ii}} \paren{b_i - \sum_{j=i+1}^{n} u_{ij}\,x_j}
$$

(**back substitution**).
Likewise, if $\matr{L}$ is lower triangular with nonzero diagonal,
$\matr{L} \vecf{y} = \vecf{b}$ has exactly one solution, given for $i = 1, \ldots, n$ by
$y_i = \frac{1}{\ell_{ii}} \paren{b_i - \sum_{j=1}^{i-1} \ell_{ij}\,y_j}$
(**forward substitution**).

:::

::: proof

Row $i$ of $\matr{U} \vecf{x} = \vecf{b}$ reads

$$
\ba
b_i
&= \sum_{j=1}^{n} u_{ij}\,x_j
&& \text{(@def-matvec-mult)}
\\
&= \sum_{j=i}^{n} u_{ij}\,x_j
&& \text{(} u_{ij} = 0 \text{ for } j < i \text{)}
\\
&= u_{ii}\,x_i + \sum_{j=i+1}^{n} u_{ij}\,x_j.
&& \text{(split off the } j = i \text{ term)}
\ea
$$

This equation is equivalent to each of

$$
\ba
u_{ii}\,x_i &= b_i - \sum_{j=i+1}^{n} u_{ij}\,x_j
&& \text{(subtract the sum from both sides)}
\\
x_i &= \frac{1}{u_{ii}} \paren{b_i - \sum_{j=i+1}^{n} u_{ij}\,x_j}.
&& \text{(divide by } u_{ii} \ne 0 \text{)}
\ea
$$

Row $n$ involves only $x_n$, so it fixes $x_n$;
once $x_{i+1}, \ldots, x_n$ are fixed, row $i$ fixes $x_i$.
So the rows, taken from the last to the first, hold exactly when $\vecf{x}$ is the vector the formula builds:
there is one solution, and only one.
For $\matr{L}$, row $i$ reads $\sum_{j=1}^{i-1} \ell_{ij}\,y_j + \ell_{ii}\,y_i = b_i$,
and the same argument runs from the first row to the last.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-back-substitution}
#### Back substitution on a $3 \times 3$ system

Solve
$\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{1}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & -1 \end{bmatrix} \vecf{x}
= \begin{bmatrix} 8 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$:

1. $x_3 = \frac{1}{-1} \cd 1 = -1$;
2. $x_2 = \frac{1}{1/2} \paren{1 - \tfrac{1}{2} \cd (-1)} = 2 \cd \tfrac{3}{2} = 3$;
3. $x_1 = \frac{1}{2} \paren{8 - 1 \cd 3 - (-1)(-1)} = \frac{1}{2} \cd 4 = 2$.

So $\vecf{x} = (2, 3, -1)$.
Without a nonzero diagonal the method fails:
$\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \vecf{x} = (1, 1)$ has no solution,
since its second row reads $0 = 1$.

:::
